constraint_decided_it: P10 falls within is declared E92 -> E92, and E93 Presence and E4 Period are both subclasses of E92, so the CRM has a declared, time-qualified containment path that neither answer used; the reference document's Spatiotemporal Relations section warns of exactly the substitute both answers chose -- 'P10 falls within (contains) is the complete inclusion of one spacetime volume in another. It should not be confused with inclusion in the spatial and temporal projection, which may be larger. E.g., in 14 AD, Mesopotamia was not within the Roman Empire.' A additionally misreports its own tool evidence: it states that 'connect E22 E4' returns no object-to-period property 'only L54 is same as', when the actual output returns P196 defines (E18 -> E92, quantified necessary) and P8 took place on or within (E4 -> E18); it likewise says connect shows only L54 for E4 -> E53 while the output shows P7 took place at declared on exactly that pair and marked necessary. That misreport is load-bearing, since it is the sole ground A gives for rejecting an object-to-period route and it conceals P196, the bridge to the better modelling.
better_modelling: Both answers get the settled part right: Sedgewick Hundred and Whitgate Rural District are each an E4 Period specialised as a geopolitical unit (Issue 312, closed 2018-01-18; E4 scope note), each with P4 has time-span, and the mill keeps one stable E53 Place via P53 has former or current location (E18 -> E53). The membership link should not be assembled from P161 projections joined by P89 falls within, because P89 (E53 -> E53) carries no temporal qualification and the projection is the union of all extents over the unit's whole existence. Instead model each episode of membership as an E93 Presence: P195 was a presence of -> the mill (E93 -> E18, necessary), P164 is temporally specified by -> an E52 Time-Span (...-1894, 1894-...), then P10 falls within -> Sedgewick Hundred / Whitgate Rural District (E92 -> E92, in domain because E93 and E4 are both E92). This is the construct Martin Doerr names in the very thread A cites (t1090, 2018-05-11: 'multiple inheritance yes, but with E92, not E53. See respective properties, they should covers all cases: P161, E93, P164'), and it yields real spatiotemporal inclusion rather than a projection overlap.
reasoning: Every property either answer applies is inside its declared domain and range (P53 E18->E53, P89 E53->E53, P161 E92->E53, P4 E2->E52, P7 E4->E53), and both reach the correct core mapping of geopolitical unit to E4 Period per Issue 312 and the E4 scope note, so neither is wrong. Both are nevertheless short of what the CRM prescribes, because they express time-varying administrative membership as untimed P89 between an E53 and a P161 projection -- precisely the confusion the reference document's Spatiotemporal Relations passage flags -- instead of E93 Presence plus P10 falls within, which Doerr points at in t1090. B's quotations all verify verbatim in t1243 and its t1093 note about F11/CRMsoc being deferred checks out, and it correctly locates the temporal information on the Periods' P4 rather than on P89, whereas A annotates its P89 edges '(valid up to 1894)' as though P89 could carry validity. A is graded unsupported rather than suboptimal because it cites search.py connect as confirming an absence that the tool does not show, and B additionally includes P7 took place at, the property declared on exactly the E4 -> E53 pair and quantified necessary, which A omits while claiming to have enumerated the routes.
